verdict.biggest_gap: A is not a night vista at all: it is an overcast-daylight combat close-up. The sky is a blown-out white-grey void with no moon, no stars and no horizon gradient, the camera sits at knee height inside a six-figure brawl so the landscape is pushed to a background strip, and the lower half of the frame is one mid-value yellow-grey grass plane with no warm accent and no fog banding, so there is no sense of scale or night atmosphere to judge.
verdict.fix: Re-stage the shot as a night wide: pull the camera back and up so a single player occupies the lower third at small scale, remove the five allies, replace the overcast skybox with a deep blue-grey gradient plus a large soft moon in the upper third, drop exposure ~2 stops to cool moonlight, add height fog with three density bands so the mountain ridges and ruins separate into distinct value steps, and put one warm point light (campfire) at the distant ruin cluster.
verdict.notes: B hits the brief as a coherent art-directed night world: dead-tree silhouettes at three depths, fog-banded ridges stepping to a pale horizon under a soft moon with faint stars, a single warm campfire at the distant ruin, and a small faceless player grounding the scale (its weak spots are the flat olive foreground grass and boxy placeholder-looking rock pillars, but the read is unmistakably the intended vista).

verdict.biggest_gap: The entire upper-right quadrant of B is blown out to flat white by an off-screen light bloom: it erases the sky gradient, swallows the right-hand pillar and torch, and collapses the night scene's value range so the frame reads as a post-process bug rather than a lit environment (compounded by a boss that is a jumble of disconnected boxes with no readable silhouette).
verdict.fix: Raise the bloom threshold and cap its intensity (or move the off-screen sun/moon disc and its volumetric glow fully out of the camera frustum) so the top-right sky holds the same navy value as the top-left; the moon already in frame should be the only bright sky source.
verdict.notes: A holds a coherent, consistently shaded night scene where the three-headed boss silhouettes cleanly against the sky, the player's long cast shadow grounds him on ground with real value variation, and the fire trail provides a single focal accent under a restrained, aligned HUD.
